details:
The downside with the current system is that you have to use both hands to do most of the gestures as the distance from the shift buttons to Fn buttons is too far. And you usually end up stopping everything you're doing in order to press it, that means you have to stop moving/jumping and physically reach your fingers over to press them.

So I've been using a gesture remapping program for desktop I made ever since gestures came out for desktop, and I've found it to be far easier to use than the current system. I'd like to suggest this new key binding and see what the community thinks. It's very easy to do and uses only one hand to perform all gestures (left and right). This leaves your right hand free to continue to use your mouse and doesn't disrupt any actions.

My suggested key remapping is as follows:

Q: Open
E: Close
R: Reset
F: Fingerpoint
1: HandGun
2: Peace
3: ThumbsUp
4: RockNRoll

If you press these keys normally, it will perform the gesture on your Right Hand, if you hold Left Shift and press it will perform it on your Left Hand.

Another additional change to the key mapping that would be very helpful for map development is that some keyboards do not have the 'menu' button required to open debug menus. A possible alternative mapping for these menu buttons would be f1 through f5, which would be freed if the gestures were remapped to my suggestion.
title: Remap gestures to be easier to use on desktop
